summary: The talk is presented jointly by Olmo Maldonado (Zapier) and Ankur Goyal (Braintrust). Zapier is a workflow automation platform with 7,000+ app integrations, processing over 10 million tasks per day. They have built multiple AI products including AI Zap Builder, Zapier Copilot, Central (a bot framework), and others. Braintrust is an end-to-end developer platform for AI teams, focused on three areas: evaluations, observability, and prompt building. Zapier was one of Braintrust's first users. The AI Zap Builder takes a user prompt and generates a Zap (automated workflow) in a single-shot approach. To measure quality, Zapier involved product managers alongside engineering to define P0 priorities: correct triggers/actions, top 25 apps supported, and internal apps like paths and filters. They built an in-house eval framework using synthetic data from their corporate account, hosted on Braintrust, run on both CI and manual bases with custom graders (logic-based and LLM-based). This grew from 7 manual unit tests to 800+ automated tests, yielding ~300% accuracy improvement. The Copilot is the next iteration: a chat interface allowing iterative interaction with the editor, functioning as an agent framework with multiple tools. Braintrust's tracing capabilities enabled granular observability into the Copilot's critical path. A key challenge emerged when migrating from GPT 3.5 Turbo to GPT-4 Turbo for the message router, trading speed for accuracy guarantees, and then to GPT-4o which caused scores to regress below 80%. Root cause analysis revealed GPT-4o was ignoring system prompts and prompts were too fine-tuned for GPT 3.5 Turbo. The resolution involved relaxing overly elaborate prompts through rapid trial-and-error iteration and deprecating the functions API in favor of tool_choice auto, with plans to experiment with tool_choice required next. After these changes, scores recovered, Zapier successfully adopted GPT-4o, and stream-based Copilot latency dropped from approximately 14 seconds to 3 seconds. Olmo concluded by expressing satisfaction with the Braintrust partnership.

sections.title: Speaker Introductions
sections.summary: Olmo Maldonado introduces himself as a 7-year Zapier engineer, husband, father, and golfer. Ankur Goyal introduces himself as Braintrust founder/CEO, formerly Head of AI at Figma and Impira founder, noting Braintrust started as a collaboration with Zapier.

sections.title: Talk Overview and Zapier Background
sections.summary: Olmo frames the talk as storytelling about what has worked at Zapier. Zapier has 7,000+ app integrations, processes 10 million tasks/day, and has built multiple AI products including AI Zap Builder, Copilot, and Central (bot framework).

sections.title: Braintrust Platform Overview
sections.summary: Ankur briefly describes Braintrust as an end-to-end developer platform used by Notion, Airtable, Instacart, Zapier, Vercel, and others, focused on three areas: evals, observability, and prompt building.

sections.title: AI Zap Builder and Eval Framework
sections.summary: Olmo explains the AI Zap Builder (single-shot Zap generation from prompts) and how they built an eval framework with Braintrust. Product managers helped define P0 priorities. They use synthetic data from corporate accounts, custom graders (logic-based and LLM-based), CI and manual runs, and observability for regression detection.

sections.title: Eval Results and Customer Reception
sections.summary: The eval suite grew from 7 manual unit tests to 800+ automated tests, improving accuracy by ~300%. Olmo shows screenshots of runs, regressions, and customer testimonials, emphasizing continuous improvement.

sections.title: Zapier Copilot and Tracing
sections.summary: The Copilot is the next iteration: a chat interface agent framework with multiple tools. Braintrust's tracing capabilities allowed granular observability into the critical path, showing inputs, outputs, tokens, and response times for chat completions.

sections.title: Model Migration Regression and Resolution
sections.summary: Zapier migrated from GPT 3.5 Turbo to GPT-4 Turbo (slower but more accurate) then to GPT-4o, which caused all scores to regress below 80%. Root cause: GPT-4o ignored system prompts and prompts were over-tuned for GPT 3.5. Fixes involved parameter adjustments to OpenAI calls, restoring prior performance.

sections.title: Resolution Details and Conclusion
sections.summary: Olmo explains how they relaxed overly elaborate prompts through rapid trial-and-error iteration and deprecated the functions API in favor of tool_choice auto, with plans to experiment with tool_choice required next. After these changes, scores recovered and Zapier adopted GPT-4o, reducing stream-based Copilot latency from ~14 seconds to ~3 seconds. Olmo concludes by expressing satisfaction with the Braintrust partnership.
